why: The 2048 measurement carried a length-bias caveat because 144 of 384 rows were refused as overlength. Qualifying a 4096 evaluation window lifted coverage to 333 of 384, which tests that caveat empirically instead of leaving it as a worry.
finding: Adding 93 longer rows moved strict accuracy from 0.2625 to 0.2553, and every other pattern replicated: the shortcut floor stayed at about 0.141, the positive control stayed at 1.0000 (333/333), false abstention on answerable worlds went 27.7 to 28.3 percent, unsupported answers on unanswerable worlds 52.9 to 51.1 percent, and the sibling-collision rate 0.2147 to 0.2056. So the 2048 length bias was SMALL in aggregate, and slightly downward as expected for longer inputs. The caveat was worth stating and is now bounded.
not_a_long_context_result: This widens an EVALUATION window on a bank whose p50 is about 1,164 native tokens. It is not a long-context claim, and both releases' length-stress splits remain unreachable on this host (11k-61k tokens, see CL-016).
one_truncation_appeared: At 4096 exactly one of 333 rows failed to terminate within the 128-token generation budget, against zero of 240 at 2048. It is counted in the denominator and not discarded.
